objective: Allow each authenticated user to archive read notifications out of the active notification center and restore them later without deleting shared notification or audit evidence.
users: Users clearing handled workflow and business notifications from the active notification center
Users recovering an accidentally archived notification
Operators preserving durable notification and audit evidence

requirements.statement: Only a read, active notification may be archived, and the archive transition must affect only the authenticated tenant and recipient while preserving the shared notification record.
acceptance: The notification disappears from the current user's ALL and UNREAD views after archive
Archiving an unread notification returns an explicit conflict
counterexample: One recipient archives the message for all recipients
An unread notification is silently archived

requirements.statement: The notification center must provide an archived view and allow a user to restore one of their archived notifications while retaining its read state.
acceptance: Archived notifications are pageable and filterable by business module
Restore returns the notification to ALL but not UNREAD
Restore is scoped to the authenticated recipient and is idempotent
requirements.source: User explicitly confirmed archived viewing and recovery on 2026-08-20 and approved the complete design on 2026-08-21.
counterexample: Restoring a notification increments the unread badge

requirements.statement: A user must be able to archive all of their active read notifications in one confirmed operation without affecting unread notifications.
acceptance: Only rows with is_read = 1 and archived_at IS NULL are changed
The API returns the actual changed count and the UI refreshes list, modules and unread count
No eligible notifications produces a zero-change success or a disabled action
counterexample: The UI clears optimistically before a failed server operation

requirements.statement: List totals, module summaries and unread counts must consistently separate active and archived notifications.
acceptance: ALL and UNREAD exclude archived rows
Module options and counts match the selected view, including modules that contain only archived rows
The one-second foreground poll remains a lightweight active unread-count request
counterexample: Archived messages remain in active module totals
A module containing only archives cannot be selected in the archived view
The polling loop reloads archived pages every second

requirements.statement: Archive and restore APIs must derive tenant and user scope from authentication and preserve existing publication, read and audit contracts.
acceptance: No archive request accepts tenantId or userId from the client
Cross-tenant and cross-user rows cannot be changed
sys_notification, publication audit and recipient rows remain durable
Existing publication, mark-read and mark-all-read clients remain compatible
requirements.source: Existing system notification contract and approved design.
counterexample: A client selects another user to archive

invariants: sys_notification remains the durable shared notification record and is never physically deleted by user archive operations
Archive state belongs to sys_user_notification and one authenticated recipient
An archived notification is always read and restore retains read state
Every query and mutation is constrained by authenticated tenant_id and user_id
Existing one-second foreground unread polling, failure backoff and notification publishing semantics remain in force
constraints: Use Java 17, Spring Boot, MySQL 8.4, Vue 3, TypeScript and Element Plus already present in the repository
Use a forward-only Flyway migration with a nullable archived_at column and supporting index
Keep legacy unreadOnly behavior when the new view parameter is absent
Implement on the local rokey branch after a separately approved implementation plan
non_goals: Administrator-driven archive or restore for another user
Automatic retention, scheduled archive or cleanup policies
External delivery channels or notification-content changes
Automatically archiving notifications when marking all as read

selected_approach.name: Recipient-scoped soft archive with archived view and restore
selected_approach.reason: It removes handled notifications from the active user experience while preserving cross-recipient isolation and durable workflow and business audit evidence.

alternatives.name: Frontend-only hiding of read notifications
alternatives.rejected_because: It cannot synchronize across devices, provide reliable recovery or keep server pagination and counts consistent.

alternatives.name: Physical deletion
alternatives.rejected_because: A notification is shared by recipients and supports business traceability, so deletion can remove evidence or affect other users.

inside: Authenticated notification list, module summary, archive, restore and bulk-archive APIs
Notification center ALL, UNREAD and ARCHIVED views
Focused service, API, build and browser verification
outside: Notification publication and workflow event content

components.name: Flyway notification archive migration
components.responsibility: Add nullable archived_at state and an index supporting authenticated active and archived queries.

components.name: SystemNotificationService
components.responsibility: Apply view filtering and recipient-scoped archive, restore and bulk archive state transitions.

components.name: NotificationController
components.responsibility: Expose backward-compatible authenticated list and module queries plus archive commands.

components.name: UiNotificationCenter
components.responsibility: Render the three views, archive eligible items, restore archives and confirm bulk archive without breaking polling or item navigation.

interfaces.name: GET /api/notifications
interfaces.contract: Accept view=ALL|UNREAD|ARCHIVED; default to ALL; preserve unreadOnly behavior when view is absent; always scope results to the authenticated recipient.

interfaces.name: GET /api/notifications/modules
interfaces.contract: Return module options and counts consistent with the requested active or archived view for the authenticated recipient.

interfaces.name: PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/archive
interfaces.contract: Archive one authenticated recipient row only when read; reject unread state explicitly; remain idempotent.

interfaces.name: PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/restore
interfaces.contract: Clear archived_at for the authenticated recipient and retain read state; remain idempotent.

interfaces.name: PATCH /api/notifications/archive-read
interfaces.contract: Archive all active read rows for the authenticated recipient and return the actual changed count.

data_flows.input: Read active notification and archive command
transitions: refresh active list and module summaries
data_flows.output: Notification hidden from active views and visible in ARCHIVED
Read notification returned to ALL without unread badge increase

transitions: reload active list, modules and unread count
data_flows.output: Handled notifications removed from the active center

error_handling.condition: Archive targets an unread active notification
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 409 with a clear read-before-archive message and retain the row unchanged.
error_handling.recovery: The user reads the notification and retries archive.

error_handling.condition: Notification is absent or outside the authenticated tenant/user scope
error_handling.behavior: Do not reveal cross-scope existence and do not modify any row.
error_handling.recovery: Refresh the current user's notification list.

error_handling.condition: Archive, restore or list request fails
error_handling.behavior: Keep the current client state, show one actionable error and avoid optimistic removal.
error_handling.recovery: Retry the operation or reload the drawer.

error_handling.condition: Business route navigation fails after a notification state change
error_handling.behavior: Show the existing route error without rolling back the durable state transition.
error_handling.recovery: Return to the notification center and retry navigation later.

security: All reads and writes include authenticated tenant_id and user_id
Archive APIs accept no client identity fields
Physical notification and audit evidence remain immutable through this feature
performance: Active unread count remains an indexed lightweight query suitable for one-second foreground polling
Archive views use a recipient and archive-state index with deterministic notification time ordering
No archived list is polled while the drawer is closed
compatibility: Legacy unreadOnly requests remain valid when view is absent
Existing publish, mark-read and mark-all-read contracts remain unchanged
Historical rows default to active because archived_at is nullable
operations: The migration requires no data backfill
Product-code rollback may leave the nullable column and index in place without behavioral impact
No destructive reverse migration is required

verification_strategy.signal: Archive and restore transitions are idempotent, tenant/user scoped and preserve shared evidence.
verification_strategy.method: Focused SystemNotificationService and controller tests with multiple users, tenants and states.

verification_strategy.signal: List totals, module summaries and unread counts remain consistent after every transition.
verification_strategy.method: Repository/service query tests plus authenticated API flow assertions.

verification_strategy.signal: The drawer exposes correct actions and views without accidental navigation or layout regressions.
verification_strategy.method: Frontend production build and desktop/mobile browser interaction with real notification data.

verification_strategy.signal: Migration and all existing notification, workflow and platform behavior remain healthy.
verification_strategy.method: Flyway startup, relevant Maven module tests, full backend tests, governance checks and diff validation.

assumptions.text: Notification and publication audit evidence must remain durable after a user cleans their active list.
assumptions.basis: Existing persistent publication audit and workflow/business notification usage.
assumptions.falsifier: A separately approved retention policy permits destructive deletion of shared notifications.

assumptions.text: A nullable archived_at timestamp is sufficient and does not require a separate boolean state.
assumptions.basis: The product needs only active versus archived plus the archive time, and one timestamp prevents dual-field inconsistency.
assumptions.falsifier: Future requirements introduce additional archive lifecycle states that cannot be represented by a timestamp.

decisions.decision: Use recipient-scoped soft archive and retain all shared notification data.
decisions.reason: The user needs a clean active list without losing audit evidence or affecting other recipients.
decisions.source: User selected option 1 and confirmed the complete design.

decisions.decision: Provide an ARCHIVED tab and single-item restore.
decisions.reason: Users must be able to inspect history and recover accidental archive actions.

decisions.decision: Archive only read notifications and provide confirmed bulk archive of all active read notifications.
decisions.reason: Unread work must not disappear, while handled backlog needs an efficient cleanup action.
Recovery is a visibility action and must not create a false unread event.

risks.risk: Module summaries can diverge from the selected notification view if the old aggregation is reused unchanged.
risks.impact: Archived-only modules may be unavailable as filters or display incorrect totals.
risks.mitigation: Make view filtering explicit in module aggregation and cover it with service and API tests.

risks.risk: Archive or restore icon clicks can bubble to the existing whole-item navigation handler.
risks.impact: Users are unexpectedly routed while managing notification state.
risks.mitigation: Use dedicated accessible icon buttons with stopped propagation and browser interaction checks.

risks.risk: Adding an index to a large target table may take operational time.
risks.mitigation: Inspect target row volume and use a MySQL 8.4-compatible forward migration; keep rollback non-destructive.

approval.evidence: The user reviewed the landed design and explicitly requested implementation on 2026-08-21.
